relationships.subject: alphaCGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: Our study showed that αCGRP deficiency led to a marked decrease of Mmp13, Adamts5, Ctsk, Tnfsf11 (Rankl), and Runx2, which further underlines the catabolic role of αCGRP for cartilage in primary OA.

relationships.subject: alphaCGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: In this study, the lifelong absence of αCGRP prevented cartilage degradation of the knee joint and decreased the expression of pro-inflammatory and catabolic cartilage markers in mice suffering from age-induced OA.

relationships.subject: alphaCGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: Yet, aged αCGRP-deficient mice showed distinct signs of tibial subchondral bone sclerosis, impaired bone quality of the epi- and metaphysis, and marked trabecular bone loss.

relationships.subject: alphaCGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: In line with these data, we detected an increased expression of SDF-1/CXCR4 signaling in WTaged mice which was not the case in aged αCGRP-deficient mice.

relationships.subject: galcanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: Treatment with galcanezumab, an antibody against CGRP, was previously not successful in human OA [14].

key_findings: Serum alphaCGRP is elevated in aged WT mice; alphaCGRP deficiency protected knee cartilage and reduced Tnfa, Il1b, Il6, Mmp13, Adamts5, Rankl expression.
alphaCGRP deficiency worsened subchondral bone sclerosis and bone loss, indicating dual pro-inflammatory and bone-protective roles.
